name: containerlab-topology-wide-interface-claim-e246
instr:
containerlab cannot detect topology-wide interface ownership conflicts before deployment using deployment's effective names and namespaces. Add atomic ownership claims, preserve link decoding and successful deploy output, and expose deterministic results during dry runs and failures.

When decoding into `links.LinkDefinition`, derive ordered claims from its `RawLink` through the existing `Link` resolution convention for every link, including node-filtered links. Keep excluded claims outside the selected transaction without changing conversion, endpoint order, or owned, consumed, and referenced semantics for veth, brief, macvlan, management-network, and host forms.

Report all effective-interface conflicts deterministically across ordinary nodes, root namespaces, host interfaces, and management bridge attachments. Permit compatible shared references and identify both topology origins for incompatible exclusive use. Atomically reconcile declared claims with node-mapped names. Release every attachment and provisional claim after failure.

`NewClaimTransaction() *ClaimTransaction`, `(*ClaimTransaction).Add(claims ...InterfaceClaim) error`, `(*ClaimTransaction).Commit() ([]InterfaceClaim, error)`, and `(*ClaimTransaction).Rollback()` must preserve topology order without partial commits. Repeated resolution must atomically replace links, endpoints, and claims. Accept deployment only for links covered by the current commit, releasing untransferred ownership after failure or cancella
